To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glomerular cell hyperplasia precedes glomerular sclerosis, and is accompanied by increased expression of PDGFB and its receptor in glomeruli.

1) glomerular proliferation of mesangium and endothelial cells precedes glomular sclerosis in the remnant model; 2) platelets may be a trigger for the onset of glomeruloproliferation; and 3), glomerular macrophages are recruited after the onset of glomular cell proliferation.

1) in the remnant model, proliferation of mesangium and endothelium is associated with glomerular fibrin deposition, platelet accumulation, PDGF expression, and monocyte/macrophages; 2) the onset of glomerulopathy is associated with glomrular fibrin deposition and platelet accumulation; and 3 ) proliferation of intrinsic cells and glomerular fibrino-gen deposition precede glomerulopathy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular events that precedes glomerular sclerosis in the 5/6 renal ablation model.
the mechanisms of progressive glomerular injury in the remnant model of chronic renal failure.
the mechanisms involved in glomerular sclerosis and the possible role of platelets, PDGF and monocytes in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glomerular proliferation precedes glomerular sclerosis in the remnant nephrectomized rat.
the glomerular proliferation is the first and the key step in the development of glomelar sclerosis in the remnant nephrectomy model.
glomerular cell growth and proliferation precede glomerular sclerosis, and that this process may be regulated by PDGF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
proliferation of intrinsic glomular cells precedes the onset of glomerulosclerosis, and may be triggered by platelet activation and mediated by PDGF released by intrinsic glomerular cell.

glomerular cell hyperproliferation is an initiating event in the development of glmerular sclerosis in the remnant model, and that platelet activation and PDGF are important in the initiation of this process.
the proliferation of intrinsic glomeular cells is the initiating event of glomerular sclerosis in the remnant model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glomerular cell growth and glomerulosclerosis are not simply two parallel events, but rather glomerular cell expansion may be a key step in the initiation and progression of glomerulosclerosis.
glomerular cell growth and PDGF expression occur prior to glomerulosclerosis and may play a role in the pathogenesis of this disease process.
proliferation of glomerular cells, and the expression of PDGF, precede glomerular scleroic changes in the remnant model.
